tokens.STACK_SUMMARY: A markdown-only meta-repository: the product is the orchestration kit itself — canonical Claude-format templates under `skills/setup/templates/` (agents, skills, loop, model map, architecture doc), per-harness emitter instructions under `skills/setup/emitters/`, and a verified harness capability matrix under `skills/setup/reference/`. Research ground truth lives in `docs/` (`docs/research-multi-harness-upgrade.md` is the canonical domain reference). The only executable code is the loop driver and circuit-breaker templates (bash + PowerShell twins), the repo's structural checks, and the self-install scripts. There is no application runtime and no test framework — verification is structural (greps, syntax checks, frontmatter validation via `(cd .claude && bash checks.sh)`).
tokens.EXECUTION_LAYERS: templates/ (canonical source) → emitters/ → reference/harness-matrix.md → docs/ + root README.md/ORCHESTRATION.md
tokens.QA_SURFACES: - **Emitted install artifacts** — the output a /setup run produces in a target project. Evidence: grep output proving zero unresolved tokens/bootstrap comments; frontmatter validation (every `name:` matches its folder/file); `bash -n` output for the emitted loop.sh; link-check output proving relative links in the emitted README/architecture doc resolve.
tokens.EVALUATOR_AUTO_FAIL_TRIGGERS:
- Unresolved '{{...}}' template token, or a leftover bootstrap comment (an HTML
  comment opening with the word BOOTSTRAP), in any emitted/instance file.
- A template token used anywhere under skills/setup/templates/ that is not documented
  in the placeholder table of skills/setup/SKILL.md.
- Frontmatter `name:` not matching its folder name (skills) or file name (agents).
- Hardcoded model IDs anywhere outside the model map (canonical:
  skills/setup/templates/models.map.md; instance: {{IDE_DIR}}/skills/setup-models.map.md).
- Instance- or session-specific content leaked INTO canonical templates — the
  canonical kit under skills/setup/ must stay project-agnostic (product isolation).
- Template ↔ emitter drift — an emitter under skills/setup/emitters/ referencing
  files, paths, or keys that no longer exist in templates/.
tokens.QA_AUTO_FAIL_TRIGGERS:

- An emitted (or canonical) loop.sh failing `bash -n`.

bootstrap.fallback-chains:
| Tier | Chain (first available wins) |
|------|------------------------------|
| `frontier` | opus → sonnet → (omit pin — harness default) |
| `light` | sonnet → haiku → (omit pin — harness default) |

Cursor fallback (same policy, Cursor IDs): `cursor-grok-4.6-xhigh` → `composer-2.5-fast`
→ (omit pin); light: `composer-2.5-fast` → (omit pin). Cursor silently substitutes a
compatible model under team-admin/plan restrictions, or when the resolved ID is
unknown/stale (a rotated-out or misspelled model name) — evaluators must report which
model produced the verdict.
bootstrap.frontier-alt-family:
| Ladder step | Model pin |
|-------------|-----------|
| Diagnosis-driven implementation attempt (rung 4) | Claude Code `opus` / Cursor `cursor-grok-4.6-xhigh` |
| Evaluator arbitration mode (rung 5) | `gpt-5.6-sol-medium` — a different model **family** from the primary evaluator at frontier tier (analytical diversity at the capability floor) |

**Claude Code note:** `gpt-5.6-sol-medium` is pinned for arbitration on both harnesses.
Claude Code accepts full cross-provider model IDs when configured in the user's
environment; if unavailable, org allowlists may ignore the pin — evaluators should
report which model produced the verdict.
bootstrap.loop-fallback:
| Chain (first available wins) | Resolves |
|-------------------------------|----------|
| sonnet → (omit pin — harness default) | `sonnet` |

Light-tier by default — the loop's iterations are implementer/test-writer-shaped work,
same as the `light` row above. Ends with the same omit-the-pin rule as the tables
above: a trip past the last chain entry clears the model pin and the harness default
takes over (no hardcoded model IDs outside this file). The resolved chain is one
comma-separated string with no spaces around commas — neither driver twin trims chain
entries.
bootstrap.models-map-caveats:
- **Claude Code env overrides**: `CLAUDE_CODE_SUBAGENT_MODEL` and
  `CLAUDE_CODE_EFFORT_LEVEL` override frontmatter; org `availableModels` allowlists can
  cause pins to be ignored.
- Model values: Claude aliases (`opus`, `sonnet`, `haiku`) or full IDs are both valid;
  `inherit` is the frontmatter default if a tier is deliberately unpinned.
- **Cursor silent fallback**: under team-admin/plan restrictions, or when the resolved
  ID is unknown/stale (a rotated-out or misspelled model name), Cursor substitutes a
  compatible model without erroring — evaluators should state their expected model in
  their prompt and report which model produced the verdict.
- **Cursor Cloud Agents** are main→L1 only; the QA-gate flow still works, but
  nested L2 worker spawns from an L1 agent are not available in cloud.
bootstrap.models-map-effort:
Reasoning-effort pins: evaluators `high`, workers `medium` — Claude Code `effort:`
frontmatter. Cursor's effort is encoded directly in the model slug for the four IDs
above (`cursor-grok-4.6-xhigh`, `composer-2.5-fast`, `gpt-5.6-sol-medium`) — no
separate `effort:` key and no bracket params on this instance (live schema verified
2026-08-21: `name`, `description`, `model`, `readonly`, `is_background` — no `tools:`
key).
bootstrap.models-map-fix-cycle:
| Fix cycle | Implementer model |
|-----------|-------------------|
| 1 | `sonnet` (normal) / Cursor `composer-2.5-fast` (normal) |
| 2 | Claude Code `opus` (single-provider — bump tier early); Cursor `gpt-5.6-sol-medium` (different family at a comparable coding tier) |
| 3 | Claude Code `opus` with effort `xhigh`; Cursor `cursor-grok-4.6-xhigh` |
bootstrap.models-map-live-check:
**Live-checked 2026-08-24**: the four Cursor model slugs below
(`cursor-grok-4.6-xhigh`, `composer-2.5-fast`, `gpt-5.6-sol-medium` — including the
post-cycle-3 arbitration pin) were confirmed present in the live Cursor model list on

bootstrap.path-test-conventions:
| Changed path | First impacted files |
|--------------|----------------------|
| `skills/setup/templates/agents/*.md` | `skills/setup/emitters/*.md` (mapping tables), `skills/setup/templates/ORCHESTRATION.md` (subagent tables) |
| `skills/setup/templates/skills/*/` | `skills/setup/emitters/*.md`, `skills/setup/templates/ORCHESTRATION.md` (skills table, file tree) |
| `skills/setup/templates/loop/*` | `skills/setup/emitters/*.md`, `skills/setup/SKILL.md` (loop extras), `skills/setup/templates/ORCHESTRATION.md` (loop section) |
| `skills/setup/templates/models.map.md` | every template using model tiers (agents, ORCHESTRATION.md), `skills/setup/SKILL.md` placeholder table |
| `skills/setup/SKILL.md` (placeholder table) | the whole `skills/setup/templates/` tree (token usage) |
| `skills/setup/emitters/*.md` | the template files that emitter maps (drift check) |
| `skills/setup/reference/harness-matrix.md` | `docs/research-multi-harness-upgrade.md`, `skills/setup/emitters/*.md` |

bootstrap.qa-surfaces-keep:
### Emitted install artifacts (the output of a /setup run in a target project)

- Zero unresolved '{{...}}' template tokens and zero leftover bootstrap comments in
  every emitted file — demonstrated by grep output over the full emitted tree.
- Every emitted agent and skill file has valid frontmatter and its `name:` matches its
  folder name (skills) or file name (agents) — demonstrated by validation output.
- The emitted `_loop/loop.sh` passes `bash -n` and is executable.
- Relative links in the emitted README section and architecture doc
  (ORCHESTRATION.md instance) resolve to real files — demonstrated by link-check
  output.
- The emitted model map is the only place model IDs appear; agent frontmatter uses the
  tiers/aliases it defines.
- The manifest (`orchestration-kit.manifest.json`) lists every emitted file with a
  correct sha256.
